summary.short: Implements Emergency Decree 007-2020 on Peru's digital trust framework. Requires public entities and digital service providers to manage digital security risks, report incidents to the national security centre, and, for listed providers, evaluate algorithms and inform people of automated decisions. Enters into force 90 calendar days after publication.
summary.long: Supreme Decree 126-2025-PCM approves the regulation of Emergency Decree 007-2020 on Peru's digital trust framework, covering digital security, personal data, transparency and consumer protection. The Secretaría de Gobierno y Transformación Digital (SGTD-PCM) is the governing body. Public entities and listed digital service providers (PSD), including financial, basic-service (electricity, water, gas), health, passenger transport, internet, critical-activity and education providers, must manage digital security risks, implement security controls and notify digital security incidents to the National Digital Security Centre (CNSD). Critical incidents must be notified within 48 hours of the provider becoming aware of them. Listed PSD must evaluate their algorithms for privacy, ethical use and human rights, and provide a channel to inform people of automated algorithm-based decisions and a way to contest them. The regulation sets up or governs the CNSD, a national incident registry, a national data centre, a digital talent platform and trust networks, and provides for monitoring and supervision by the SGTD-PCM. It does not itself set fines; Article 21(k) refers non-compliance to the competent supervisory authority. Entry into force is 90 calendar days after publication.

notes: The decree is a regulation of DU 007-2020 and the registry does not list that DU, so target_instrument_id is left blank. Article count and structure (preliminary title, Títulos I-III, nine chapters, 42 articles, nine Disposiciones Complementarias Finales) match Art. 1 of the decree. Art. 29.2 says 'Registro Nacional de Incidencias de Seguridad Digital' while Art. 29.1 and elsewhere say 'Registro Nacional de Incidentes de Seguridad Digital'. Art. 5.1 defines PSD as any public entity or private organisation, but Art. 14.1 and Art. 18.1 apply several duties only to listed sectors. Art. 25.1 refers to the 'Marco de Seguridad Digital' where Art. 6 uses 'Marco de Confianza Digital'. Entry into force is 90 days after publication (Disposición Complementaria Final Única).

thresholds.note: No numeric cutoff that changes legal treatment was found. Procedural time limits (48 hours in Art. 32.1; 120 and 90 business days in the Final Provisions) are events, not thresholds. Authentication assurance levels (Art. 17.1, one or two factors) are technical specifications that do not decide scope or eligibility. The critical-incident classification (Art. 32.2 and Art. 33) is delegated to SGTD-PCM without a numeric value. Entry into force after 90 calendar days (Disposición Complementaria Final, Única) is a phase-in date, not a threshold.
